scope: All pinned upstream Git and Git LFS commands, including commands without a convenience API. A scope is complete when it meets the completion criterion below; finite native corpora witness its obligations but never establish completeness on their own.

criterion: Every facet has evidence. Only operand-grammar and combination-rules may instead be listed in inapplicableFacets, with a reason.

A closure exists for the pinned Git baseline. It names its entry point and the audited source functions; every same-file function that a listed function calls or references (option callbacks included) is listed too or waived with a reason, which command-coverage checks against spec/upstream/git-refusal-sites.json.

Every refusal site extracted from the listed functions (scripts/refusal-sites.mjs; snapshot spec/upstream/git-refusal-sites.json, reproduced from the pinned source by verify-upstream.mjs) is named by exactly one refusal obligation, and every named site exists in the snapshot.
The closure also has at least one obligation for each of parser, values, operands, state and platform, and at least one modeled obligation.

Every obligation is modeled (with repository evidence files), delegated to native Git at runtime (with a reason and a basis naming the runtime input), or excluded under a declared exclusion that covers its kind. Refusal sites are never excluded. No obligation is open.
The free-text remaining field is empty; narrative moves to notes.

other-git-versions.reason: A closure is a claim about the pinned baseline only. Behavior of other Git releases, including the legacy 2.25.1 job, is witnessed by regression tests but is not part of the claim, and a baseline change reopens every closure.

commit.notes: Ordinary source-table option parsing, native long prefixes/negations, short clusters, LASTARG_DEFAULT, consumed end markers and help timing are modeled. Column token grammar/enable projection, empty object-name callbacks, untracked-file boolean grammar and selected final cleanup/column conflicts are checked against 9,805 independent Git outcomes across branch/tag/status/commit. Empty pathspec operands are rejected after option parsing, as parse_pathspec does in prepare_index, including dry-run and status-format modes, while help exits first. Only mode without path operands or a pathspec option is rejected unless --allow-empty, --amend or an amend: fixup is active, which matches prepare_index; --amend with a plain fixup is delegated to native Git, because Git 2.32 and later refuse it but older Git accepts it; it counts pathspec.nr after parse_pathspec_file reads the file, so only the presence of the pathspec option is modeled. repo.commit emits no paths, so its include mode is rejected without a nonempty pathspecFromFile and its only mode uses the same exemptions, and its reword: fixups are rejected with include, only or all, as runtime checks. These cases are checked against 411 independent Git 2.55.0 dry-run outcomes in test/fixtures/status-commit-path-corpus.json, covering -o/--only/--no-only, last-wins --allow-empty, --amend and --fixup negations, empty and amend: fixups, a pathspec file and empty operands, and every refusal from these rules is reached with its native diagnostic. The executing Git is compared in src/commands/status-commit-paths.test.ts, with the pathspec-file and fixup-prefix cases gated for the legacy Git 2.25.1 job. --reset-author without -C, -c or --amend is valid during an in-progress cherry-pick or rebase pick, so it is delegated to native Git. Pathspec files that name no paths, or cannot be opened, fail natively and are delegated to native Git. Author nickname lookup, amend and merge state, -C/-c/--fixup/--squash object resolution, pathspec file contents, pathspec magic and other configuration/repository state are delegated to native Git at runtime. --fixup suboptions (an ASCII-letter prefix before ':') must be amend or reword in the typed API and in repo.commit, and repo.commit refuses an amend: or reword: fixup with a message at runtime. The closure leaves three obligations open: the --author ident grammar, the --date grammar, and the only-mode refusal for --amend with a plain fixup (kept accepted for Git before 2.32) together with pathspec files that name no paths. Other callbacks, completion and other parser modes remain separate audit obligations. The finite corpus and deterministic representative-state exploration do not establish completeness.

merge.notes: The ordinary native option pass models long-prefix resolution, short clusters, consumed end markers and retained operands, and OPTION_INTEGER storage and lexical semantics for --log follow the recorded Git 2.55 compiler/libc profile. The closure corpus runs every case in a fresh repository and counts a refusal as state-dependent only when the same argv succeeds with its named operands replaced by a diverged branch, a fast-forward branch, the current branch or -, or during a conflicted merge, or when it depends on signatures, keys, upstream configuration or unrelated histories; a missing strategy or message file stops parsing, so such a case is state-dependent only when the same argv with an existing strategy and file is; the wrapper must accept exactly the argv that some such state accepts. -X values and an empty -m are therefore left to Git: they are refused only when a strategy runs or a merge commit is written.

pull.remaining: Pull forwards its fetch options and its repository and refspec words to fetch: 383 independent Git 2.55.0 cases cover the forwarded final --depth and --jobs values, every forwarded --deepen word, OPT_INTEGER suffix, hexadecimal and int-range boundaries, the deepen/depth/unshallow combinations, --all with a repository, and fetch's reinterpretation of dash-prefixed forwarded operands. Because pull drops its own -- before forwarding, dash-prefixed pull operands are rejected even after -- (a type-git restriction: Git runs them as fetch options, for example --upload-pack). A valueless --jobs or -j is rejected as well, since fetch consumes the next forwarded word as its value, and the native successes where that word is a numeric repository operand are recorded in the corpus. Pull's own pass is modeled with the native option tables, the pull-rebase and fetch-recurse callbacks and the final cleanup check. In Git 2.25.1 pull has no --deepen, --shallow-since, --shallow-exclude, --server-option or negotiation options, so native Git rejects them as unknown options there. The forwarded --jobs value is checked with the selected integer profile, so the 2.25.1 strtol conversion and the 2.55.0 suffix grammar are both modeled. A Git 2.25.1 native run of this corpus is not yet recorded. An invalid --deepen value followed by a pull help exit is refused at the value although Git prints usage; that ordering is not yet modeled. Remote names, URLs, refspec and refmap syntax, transport depth syntax such as 1x and remote resolution of words such as - are delegated to native fetch at runtime. The merge or rebase phase (strategy, squash, commit, ff, log, signoff and gpg-sign values and combinations) is reached only after a successful non-dry-run fetch with merge candidates and is selected by configuration and fast-forward state, so it is delegated to native git merge and git rebase. Repository/configuration state, abbreviations and completion remain separate obligations. Boolean callback literal and normalized-state grammars share source-backed profiles and a finite independent Git corpus. Finite native outcomes do not establish completeness.

switch.remaining: Native ordinary option tables, prefixes/negations, short clusters, callback/help timing and retained operand separators are modeled. Checkout scans for the first --; reset recognizes it only at index 0 or 1; switch/restore consume the initial marker. 7,902 independent Git 2.55.0 outcomes across the four commands cover these distinctions, including literal subsequent markers and dash-prefixed refs/paths. An empty start point is rejected in every switch mode ("invalid reference"), and an empty -c/-C/--orphan name fails the branch-name check; both are covered by Git 2.55.0 corpus cases, follow a help exit, and repo.switch rejects an empty target before running Git. Whether a nonempty target names a branch, a remote-tracking guess or a commit, and whether a nonempty new name passes check-ref-format, depend on repository state or the full ref-name grammar and are delegated to native Git at runtime, as are configuration, worktree state and conflicts. The typed builder requires an explicit -- before a dash-prefixed operand, so a literal --end-of-options operand is refused as a type-git policy rather than a Git rule. Completion and other parser modes remain open. Finite corpus and representative-state exploration are not completeness evidence. Existing independently selected source/ABI/callback profiles, original argument context and literal-union safety remain retained; other parser profiles remain partial.

stash create.notes: The child performs no option parsing: every word after create is joined with single spaces into the message (Git 2.55.0 builtin/stash.c:create_stash), so dash-prefixed words, --help, -- and --end-of-options are message text, while option and separator tokens and NUL are rejected. 190 independent Git 2.55.0 runs (scripts/stash-create-corpus.mjs; 95 word sequences in clean and modified worktrees), each recorded as a direct and a root-dispatched wrapper case (380 cases), cover help, completion, terminator, typo, cluster, unknown-option, empty and repeated-empty, space, non-ASCII (é) and TAB/LF/CR/U+0001 words on Linux; all exit 0, a clean tree creates nothing and a modified tree stores "On <branch>: <joined words>" or the WIP message for an empty join (checked by the generator), and the wrapper accepts and serializes every case unchanged. The corpus is finite and does not prove completeness over all message words. Git 2.25.1 instead runs an empty parent parse_options pass over the whole argv first, which before a -- or --end-of-options exits 129 for -h-prefixed words, --help, --help-all and single-dash -no- typo words; these legacy exits are covered by runtime witnesses that leave the exit to the selected Git and were rechecked against a Git 2.25.1 build. Whether a commit is created depends on tracked index/worktree changes and remains delegated to native Git: a clean tree exits 0 with no output, while a tracked file that is only stat-dirty (rewritten with unchanged content) exits 1 with no output in 2.55.0, 2.25.1 and 2.43.0, because the quick tracked-change check sees the stat change and the refreshed index then has nothing to stash; a runtime witness compares that exit with native Git. An unborn HEAD and core.trustctime/core.checkStat, which change what counts as stat-dirty, are likewise delegated without a witness. The closure over create_stash and do_create_stash delegates repository-state, filesystem and platform behavior to native Git.
